title: [VSC-13] VS Code: AccountPresentation port that passes the shared accounts corpus
description:
Epic epic-aabc654d (VS Code works + plugin reuse), sliced by task-a3e414a3 (VSC-0). Depends on VSC-7 (task-93729f32ef6f408cbd411813c5c93838: moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-accounts.json, a held-out corpus this row must pass UNCHANGED) and VSC-12 (task-daf5abdd282a4c46b280eb0a48e74cd9: moe-vscode/src/types/accounts.ts and the client's accountRotation).

Objective: a pure TypeScript port of JetBrains' AccountPresentation.kt (rows, chips, actions, isValidLabel) whose text is `{ key, args }` exactly as the corpus writes it, plus an English resolver for those keys that matches moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties (VSC-0's shared-strings rule).

Deliverable: new moe-vscode/src/util/AccountPresentation.ts (pure: no vscode import and no runtime import at all; the time and zone are parameters, as in the corpus) and new moe-vscode/tests/accounts-corpus.test.cjs that loads the module under node:vm with a require map that throws on every name (tests/managed-vm.test.cjs loads the pure ManagedVm.ts this way), runs every corpus row and label case, and checks the resolver's text for every key in the corpus against MoeBundle.properties with {0}-style args substituted.

Not in scope: the tree view, commands and package.json (VSC-14, VSC-15), any moe-jetbrains file, the corpus.

Verification (GLOBAL rail: never npm in the shared checkout): `git archive HEAD` of the whole repo into a fresh directory outside the checkout, overlay this task's files, then in <snapshot>/moe-vscode run `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm run lint && npm run compile && npm test` under `env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin` (mem:gotcha-vscode-gate-from-wsl).
definitionOfDone: moe-vscode/tests/accounts-corpus.test.cjs runs every rotation row of client-accounts.json through AccountPresentation.ts's rows, chips and actions with the corpus' fixed now and zone, and every label case through isValidLabel; all pass, with failing ids reported together.
The test checks that the English the resolver gives for every key used in the corpus equals the value in moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties, args substituted.
AccountPresentation.ts loads under a require map that throws on every module name and contains no vscode reference.
client-accounts.json and every moe-jetbrains file are unchanged by this task's diff.
In a git-archive snapshot of HEAD plus this diff, `cd moe-vscode && npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm run lint && npm run compile && npm test` exits 0 with 0 failures.

implementationPlan.description:
Write moe-vscode/tests/accounts-corpus.test.cjs FIRST, with the Write tool; it is red until steps 2-3 land.
- Load moe-vscode/src/util/AccountPresentation.ts the way tests/managed-vm.test.cjs loads ManagedVm.ts: ts.transpileModule (CommonJS, ES2020), then `vm.runInThisContext('(function (exports, module, require) {' + code + '\n})')` with a require that throws on EVERY name (DoD 3). Objects then live in the test realm, so deepStrictEqual works.
- Assert that the TS source has no match for `/\bvscode\b/`.
- The corpus is `path.join(__dirname, '../../moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-accounts.json')`, landed by VSC-7 (task-93729f32, plan revision 1): `{ version: 1, now: "2026-10-20T12:00:00.000Z", zone: "UTC", rows: [ { id C01..C15, note, rotation (daemon AccountRotationView wire JSON or null), selectedId, connected, expectRows: [ { id, position, label, signIn, fiveHour, weekly, status, vmToken } ], expectChips: [ text ], expectActions: { the 12 booleans } } ], labels: [ { id L01..L14, input, valid } ] }`, where a text is `{ key, args }` and args are JSON strings or integers.
- Never edit the corpus or any moe-jetbrains file.
Its error handling: an unreadable corpus or bundle fails naming the path; per-row checks collect `<id>: ...` and end in one assert, so all failing ids show at once.
Tests:
1. `every rotation row renders through the port`: now = Date.parse(corpus.now), zone = corpus.zone.
   - rotation = AP.parseAccountRotation(row.rotation); a non-null corpus rotation must parse to non-null;
   - deepStrictEqual AP.rows(rotation, now, zone) with expectRows, AP.chips(rotation, now, zone) with expectChips, and AP.actions(rotation, row.selectedId, row.connected) with expectActions;
   - require version 1 and at least 12 rows.
2. `every label case follows the daemon rule`: AP.isValidLabel(input) === valid for every label row (at least 8).
3. `the resolver speaks MoeBundle English`: parse moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties as UTF-8 with `/^(moe\.accounts\.[A-Za-z.]+)=(.*?)\r?$/gm`.
   - (a) For every text in the corpus (row texts and chips), AP.resolveAccountText(text) equals the bundle value with each {n} replaced by String(args[n]).
   - (b) Every key in AP.ACCOUNT_TEXT equals the bundle's raw value, so keys that VSC-14 and VSC-15 add later stay pinned.
   - (c) No such value contains a single quote, so a plain substitution equals Java MessageFormat.

Gate in fresh Linux-native snapshots. Never run npm or node tests in the shared checkout (GLOBAL rail; mem:gotcha-vscode-gate-from-wsl). Use the checkRef's env -i PATH for every node and npm call.
1) Red/green: build a snapshot as the checkRef does, but overlay only tests/accounts-corpus.test.cjs. Run `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund`, then `node --test tests/accounts-corpus.test.cjs`. It must FAIL: the module is missing at HEAD. Then overlay AccountPresentation.ts and rerun: it passes.
2) Mutant, in that snapshot copy only: change actions' moveUp condition from `index > 0` to `index >= 0`, with an exact-string replace asserted to hit once. The focused test must fail naming C04, C06, C11 and C13, the same rows as VSC-7's JetBrains mutant. Then discard the snapshot.
3) Run the checkRef verbatim (a new snapshot). Confirm exit 0 and 0 failures, and report the test count.
Error handling for a red run:
- A row the port cannot meet means either a port slip (re-read the Kotlin first) or JetBrains being wrong.
- Never edit the corpus and never bend the port to it. For a genuine JetBrains bug, comment on task-93729f32 with moe.add_comment, naming the row, and stop.
- A failure tied to a peer's wip checkpoint follows mem:gotcha-snapshot-gate-peer-wip-checkpoint.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: moe-vscode/src/util/AccountPresentation.ts is a pure TypeScript port of JetBrains' account parse and presentation: parseAccountRotation (MoeJson rules), rows, chips, actions and isValidLabel, with text as { key, args } exactly as client-accounts.json writes it, plus an English resolver equal to MoeBundle.properties. tests/accounts-corpus.test.cjs replays the held-out corpus unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: Every rotation row of client-accounts.json renders through parseAccountRotation, rows, chips and actions with the corpus' now and zone, and every label case through isValidLabel; failing ids are reported together.
resolveAccountText gives the bundle English, args substituted, for every corpus text, and every ACCOUNT_TEXT template equals its bundle value.
AccountPresentation.ts loads under a require that throws on every name and has no match for /\bvscode\b/.
The moveUp-at-index-0 mutant fails C04, C06, C11 and C13.
invariants: AccountPresentation.ts has no import statement and no vscode reference; time and zone are parameters.
client-accounts.json, MoeBundle.properties, every moe-jetbrains file, MoeDaemonClient.ts and src/types/* are unchanged.
No function throws for any input; parsed windows live in a Map.
No npm or node test command runs in the shared checkout.
compatibility: A later caller (VSC-14) passes client.accountRotation through parseAccountRotation and then rows; nothing else in the extension changes.
approvedScope: AccountPresentation.ts exports: AccountText, PresentedAccount, PresentedRotation, MAX_ACCOUNTS, MAX_LABEL_LENGTH, parseAccountRotation, rows, chips, actions, isValidLabel, ACCOUNT_TEXT, resolveAccountText.
Row, chip and action objects use the corpus member names exactly.
reuse: tests/managed-vm.test.cjs: the runInThisContext pure-module loader with a throwing require.
VSC-8's delivery-corpus.test.cjs: the MoeBundle.properties regex reading.
sourceAssumptions: VSC-7 (task-93729f32, plan revision 1) lands client-accounts.json as generated by its oracle: 15 rows C01..C15 and 14 labels L01..L14, now 2026-10-20T12:00:00.000Z, zone UTC; L08 'a\u0085b' is valid after VSC-7 fixes JetBrains' isValidLabel.
moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/AccountPresentation.kt and moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/MoeJson.kt parseAccountRotation define the semantics ported.
packages/moe-daemon/src/accounts/registry.ts CONTROL_CHARS_RE = /[\u0000-\u001f\u007f]/ with JS trim is the label rule.
VSC-12 (task-daf5abdd) gives the client an accountRotation holding the wire payload; this module needs no import from it, because parseAccountRotation accepts unknown.
checkRefs: R=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel) && cd "$R" && S=$(mktemp -d -t vsc13-gate-XXXXXX) && git archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$S" && cp --parents moe-vscode/src/util/AccountPresentation.ts moe-vscode/tests/accounts-corpus.test.cjs "$S/" && cd "$S/moe-vscode" && umask 022 && env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" bash -c 'npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm run lint && npm run compile && npm test'

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: The parse lives in the pure module because MoeDaemonClient.ts cannot take a value import (closed require maps), and the corpus feeds raw wire rotations. VSC-12's client keeps the payload; this module normalizes it for display. Rejected: importing VSC-12's types (still unplanned; coupling for no gain). Rejected: a resolver covering all 72 AccountKeys now (YAGNI). Test 3(b) pins whatever keys later rows add. Time formatting uses Intl with hourCycle h23 (avoids the 24:00 quirk), and the zone is a parameter so tests are deterministic.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: The managed-vm loader (runInThisContext) keeps module objects in the test realm, so deepStrictEqual against the corpus works directly. JS object key order matches Gson/LinkedHashMap order for non-integer keys such as five_hour and seven_day. Kotlin maxByOrNull keeps the first maximum. Corpus timestamps use the daemon's toISOString form (.000Z), and C13's 'soon' must pass through unchanged.
planningNotes.risks: dependsOn VSC-7 and VSC-12: the worker can claim only after both are DONE. Leading or trailing U+001C..U+001F and U+FEFF trim differently in Kotlin and JS; the corpus avoids them (mem:decision-client-corpus-conventions). Java MessageFormat would group numbers of 1000 or more; the corpus numbers stay small, so a plain String(arg) substitution is exact there. HEAD can carry a peer's red wip checkpoint (mem:gotcha-snapshot-gate-peer-wip-checkpoint).
